definition: Biotransport refers to the movement and distribution of a biological substance within the body. In this source, it specifically means how nitric oxide is produced, diffuses through brain tissue and blood vessel cells, and is reduced through reactions with other molecules.

reasons: The first sentence generalizes biotransport as the movement and distribution of a biological substance within the whole body, but the packet only supports a brain NO transport model, not a general body-wide definition.

The phrase "through brain tissue and blood vessel cells" is not stated in the packet; the source mentions diffusion in the brain and NO production in neurons and endothelial cells, but not transport through blood vessel cells as such.

The definition’s first sentence gives a broad, general meaning (“movement and distribution of a biological substance within the body”) that is not explicitly supported in the provided packet text, which instead frames the topic specifically as modeling nitric oxide (NO) transport/biotransport in the brain.

The packet supports the NO-related specifics (production in neurons and mechanotransduction in endothelial cells, diffusion/anomalous diffusion in the brain, and loss/reduction via reactions with superoxide and interaction with hemoglobin), but it does not substantiate the general biological-substance distribution phrasing as the source’s meaning.
